body:
MECHANISM 1 IS CONFIRMED. THE MEASUREMENT EXISTS AND IT SAYS CRLF.

    BUG-1555 line-ending probe on Windows
    core.autocrlf = true            <- the precondition, never before observed
    core.eol      = (unset)
    --- the two sides the drift test compares ---
      project copy: CRLF  (.aida/discipline/README.md)
      master      : LF    (aida-core/templates/.aida/discipline/README.md)
    --- every tracked project-copy guide ---
      ALL 26 .md guides: CRLF

    ...and in the same job:
    test templates::tests::project_discipline_pack_matches_master ... FAILED
    957 passed; 1 failed

BOTH ARMS, ONE RUN:

    macOS    autocrlf unset   project LF   master LF   test PASSES
    Windows  autocrlf true    project CRLF master LF   test FAILS

That is the whole mechanism, end to end, measured rather than inferred:
`.gitattributes` pins `aida-core/templates/**` to `eol=lf` and says nothing
about `.aida/discipline/**`; Windows checkout with autocrlf=true writes the
project copy CRLF; `local.trim_end() != *master` normalises trailing
whitespace only, so every interior newline differs and all compared files
fail together.

THE PREDICTION WAS REGISTERED BEFORE THE READING AND IT HELD. I said I would
send it either way and that LF on both sides would FALSIFY mechanism 1 and
return BUG-1555 to no surviving cause. It did not come back LF. The
falsification condition was real and it was not met.

ONE PRECISION, AND IT IS MY OWN FINDING BITING IMMEDIATELY: THE PROBE DID NOT
MEASURE glossary.yaml. Its loop globs `*.md`, so of the 23 files the drift
test actually compares, 22 are .md and measured CRLF directly, and
glossary.yaml — the 23rd, and one of the files in the nightly's failure list —
is INFERRED from the same checkout rule rather than observed. I do not think
it is in doubt; I am recording it because "23 of 23 confirmed" would overstate
what this run shows, and because it is the exact gap I flagged on #2050 four
hours ago showing up in the first result that used the probe.

Glob the directory, not the extension — and then the number is 23 of 23
measured.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS: the fix can now be CREDITED rather than shipped as
hygiene. Two-sided normalisation, two-sided trim, and pinning
`.aida/discipline/**` in `.gitattributes` are the cause's remedy, not
defence-in-depth of an unknown. The ledger's standing instruction — "NOT to be
recorded as fixing this bug unless the cause is shown to be line endings" —
is now satisfied.

MY SHARPENED DEMONSTRATE-IT CRITERION STILL STANDS AND MATTERS MORE NOW, not
less: the fix must be shown to still FAIL on a real content edit AND to pass a
CRLF-only change. A normaliser that erases everything would make this test
green forever and look identical to a correct fix from the nightly's point of
view — and after today, green on that leg will be read as success by everyone.

ALSO FROM THIS RUN: macOS completed fully GREEN. First macOS-green
cross-platform run I have seen today, and a data point against BUG-1556's
arrival-rate thesis rather than for it.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: BUG-1555 SOLVED: autocrlf=true, project copy CRLF, master LF, test fails - macOS control LF/LF and passes. Mechanism 1 confirmed. Caveat: glossary.yaml inferred, not measured (the .md glob)
